title: Blockbench-authored Hytale stained-glass pilot with native-material and visual acceptance gates
summary: Adaptive Window 0.3.2 for released Hytale 0.6.8 uses one fixed BlendLinear surface containing the complete original RGBA stained-glass design, padded without resampling to native-compliant dimensions. Static/native tests pass, saved materials are retained, and the user confirmed transparency plus precise compact design in the main Zytale Working Copy.
problem_class: game-model authoring and scoped pilot integration
problem_description: Replace an oversized incomplete lancet with a real editable Hytale model and test one instance before mass placement.
context: Only Zytale Working Copy root 236,130,224; actual user screenshots expose previous incomplete glazing. No Computer Use, no mass replacement.
constraints: No client visual claim from editor or server validation
No colored-light projection claim from emission or PhysicalMaterial alone
No replacement of other windows until pilot accepted
One uniform color per diamond; four-color regular alternation
Glazing mask and stone arch must share the same profile

solution_versions.description: Author in real Blockbench Hytale format, export through codec, preserve editable source, compare installed native window data, and integrate one bounded pilot before any family expansion.
changes: 78 nodes and 384x256 atlas at 32px/block; plugin limit 255 respected
Glass alpha quad double-sided and behind tracery; frame and lead opaque; no Light/fullbright
One partition function drives both per-diamond color and lead; 4-color alternation along both axes
Correct glazing cutout to use the same dimensions as the modeled outer arch, overlapping below stone
Inspect actual native Glass/Window properties and assert runtime packet
Preview and replace one root; native engine maintains 20 fillers; verify 6553600 cells and fluids
Merge only 2 chunk records, restoring source entity sections; verify untouched files before and after install
advantages: Pilot keeps failures local and reversible
Separates data/geometry compliance from graphical approval
disadvantages: Single composite object has no independently breakable pane/frame
Native Glass material is not evidence of colored optical projection
Engine/client visual acceptance still requires real screenshots or player review
test_results: 78 nodes, zero plugin issues and UV bounds errors
53 diamond cells, 6272 sampled pixels: uniform cell colors and no equal adjacent colors
13182 clear-aperture pixels: zero transparent gaps after user correction
Native save/restart and merged-file restart: exactly 21 changed cells, no unexpected changes
1022 unrelated region records and 5551 other live files identical
0.1.1 only changes PNG and manifest; model and definitions byte-identical
Client visual, optical/light transmission and player collision tests remain UNVERIFIED

solution_versions.description: Revision 0.2.0 of the existing Blockbench stained-glass pilot: one complete 3x7x1 placeable assembly with native donor-textured masonry, using Adaptive Surface sampling and static material states. No wall excavation or restoration.
changes: Real Blockbench/Hytale export revised to 163 nodes, 32px/block, 384x256 atlas; masonry closes jambs, spandrels and header
Glass alpha reduced to 90/255; ordered alternating diamonds preserved
Six reserved atlas slots receive donor-face textures; glass and carved frame are unchanged across all variants
Reuse TextureSampler and WorldMaterialScanner from Adaptive Surface; aliases resolve native cube/stair sources; no changes to the original Adaptive Surface mod
Use matching per-click interaction sync data; fallback ray explicitly traverses air (id == 0) for installed 0.6.8
Preload 59 states and 76 textures with 899 donor aliases, no runtime asset registration
Pending generated ZIP promoted at next plugin construction, before asset ZIPs are opened
Update only packs/config in live Working Copy; no region or player data writes
advantages: One inventory item, ordinary native multipart placement and removal
Only wall surround changes material; full assembly fits one 21-cell opening
No destructive donor cutting or stored reconstruction journal
disadvantages: Requires a prepared 3x7x1 opening; not a one-unit cube
Cannot promise arbitrary mod materials; new compatible materials may need restart and must fit 8-million-pixel pack budget
Individual donor rotation/random texture choice not reproduced exactly
Single composite physical/opacity properties; no independent stone/glass break behavior or proven colored light projection
Client alpha rendering, physical player collision, performance and aesthetics remain unverified
test_results: Blockbench Hytale validator: 163/255 nodes, valid, zero issues
6272 diamond samples, 53 cells: uniform/alternating; 13182 aperture pixels without gaps; 50044 front/back wall section samples without exterior gaps
All 76 generated atlases preserve glass/frame pixels exactly and use opaque masonry pixels
Native create test: 265 checks, 8 placements, 7 donor materials, 4 yaw rotations, one item consumed, donor unchanged, no runtime asset registration
Native reload test: 24 checks for state/filler persistence, ordinary multipart removal and untouched donors
Full isolated map stage starts with existing mods, loads 899 aliases and shuts down normally; supplemental bridge RPC blocked by network sandbox and not counted as passed
Live installation changed only config and prior model ZIP, added two packs, retained 5559 other existing files byte-identical
Complete real-client new-material learning lifecycle and visual fidelity still pending user review

solution_versions.description: 0.3.0 standalone Adaptive Window corrects native glazing-face transparency and oversized held representation while preserving saved window IDs and donor materials.
changes: Enable transparent=true on the actual glazing CubeFace in Blockbench; export with the installed Hytale codec
Explicit Item.Model/Texture and Item.Scale=0.12; placed CustomModelScale=1 on base and every material state
Rename en-US/it-IT inventory label to exactly 3x7x1_window; retain internal ID and 59 original variant IDs
One distributable JAR embeds complete asset ZIP, expands/enables one authoritative cache before asset loading; no dependency on Adaptive Surface or MonasticAssets
Migrate prior cache by merging additional states/textures, keeping current geometry/name/held settings; preserve previous cache backup
Installer scopes one save, validates old package identities, backs up removed packages/config/cache, checks game both before backup and before mutation
advantages: Fixes two independently identified data defects without changing window design
Standalone download with automatic cache provisioning and next-start material learning
Existing inventory/window IDs and map files preserved
disadvantages: Client visual acceptance still pending; server flags do not prove final rendering or first-person framing
Automatic cache file remains a saved-world dependency after placing windows
One combined physical material; no independent stone/glass breaking or proven colored light projection
Future game versions require native schema/rendering revalidation
test_results: User video inspected: 2.57s, oversized held object obscures view; no new client recording produced
Actual Blockbench inspection found south glass face transparent=false; real codec exports front.transparent=true after fix
149 release checks: only one glazing face flagged, semantic model unchanged otherwise, 76 atlas byte-identical, 59 variant IDs preserved, exact name and scales
270 native create checks, 24 reload/removal checks, new-material request and 901 next-start retention/activation checks on final JAR
Full isolated map migrated and booted; bridge confirms native Glass, transparent opacity/blending, world scale=1, no emission
Live install preserved 5564 other files; old model pack and 0.2 plugin recoverably moved into backup; no world data edits
Hytale client transparency, held-item field of view and aesthetics still require user confirmation
